name: ImpresU
question: Does methenamine hippurate reduce antibiotic-treated recurrent urinary tract infections versus placebo in women aged at least 70 years?

design.population: 289 women aged at least 70 years with at least two UTI antibiotic courses in six months or three in twelve months were randomized through general practices in Norway, Sweden, Poland and the Netherlands.
design.description: Multinational, triple-blind, placebo-controlled phase 4 randomized trial
design.locator: Primary article, journal pp1874–1875, Methods and Results (Participants), Fig. 1

verdictNote: The primary mITT analysis met significance; the complete-case sensitivity analysis did not.
takeaway: In women aged at least 70 years with recurrent UTI, six months of methenamine hippurate reduced antibiotic-treated UTI incidence versus placebo (adjusted IRR 0.75, 95% CI 0.57–1.0; P = 0.049); incidence was higher in the former methenamine arm after treatment ended.

reports.label: Six-month placebo-controlled efficacy report
reports.citation: Heltveit-Olsen SR, Arnljots ES, Sundvall PD, et al. "Methenamine hippurate as prophylaxis for recurrent urinary tract infections in older women—a triple-blind, randomised, placebo-controlled, phase IV trial (ImpresU)." *Clin Microbiol Infect.* 2025;31(11):1873-1879. doi:10.1016/j.cmi.2025.07.006
reports.followUp: Six months of treatment and six months after treatment cessation
reports.followUpLocator: Primary article, journal pp1873–1874, Abstract and Methods (Study design)

results.measure: Number of antibiotic courses for UTI during six months of treatment; adjusted incidence rate ratio (IRR), methenamine versus placebo; mITT with imputation
results.note: Episodes required at least 14 symptom-free days between them. Negative binomial regression adjusted for age, local estrogen treatment, diabetes, previous urinary tract stone, baseline urease-producing bacteria and urine pH. The CI upper bound is rounded to 1.0 in the report.
results.locator: Primary article, journal p1875, Results (Primary outcome); p1877, Table 2

results.measure: Per-protocol sensitivity analysis during six months of treatment; adjusted incidence rate ratio (IRR)
results.note: 217 participants in the per-protocol analysis; arm-specific counts are not given in Table 2.

results.measure: Complete-case sensitivity analysis during six months of treatment; adjusted incidence rate ratio (IRR)
results.note: 271 participants in the complete-case analysis; arm-specific counts are not given in Table 2.

results.endpoint: Antibiotic-treated symptomatic UTI after stopping study drug
results.measure: Number of antibiotic courses for UTI during the subsequent six drug-free months; adjusted incidence rate ratio (IRR), former methenamine versus former placebo; mITT with imputation
results.note: Between-arm comparison during the off-treatment period, not a within-person change from the treatment period.
results.locator: Primary article, journal p1875, Results (Secondary outcomes); p1877, Table 2

harms.label: Serious adverse events
harms.note: Fourteen serious adverse events were equally distributed across arms; all were deemed unrelated or unlikely to be related to study treatment. These are event counts, not participant counts.

harms.label: Serious adverse events related or possibly related to UTI
harms.note: Six of the fourteen serious adverse events were related or possibly related to a UTI.

harms.label: Bladder irritation
harms.note: The only side effect reported as more frequent with methenamine; the main article gives no arm counts.

delivery.label: Study regimen

values.exp: Methenamine hippurate 1 g twice daily for six months
values.ctl: Matching placebo one tablet twice daily for six months

delivery.locator: Primary article, journal p1874, Methods (Study design)

delivery.label: Study-drug adherence

values.exp: 26/144 took less than 80% of study medication
values.ctl: 28/145 took less than 80% of study medication

delivery.note: The article prints 26 (9.0%) and 28 (9.7%) using all 289 randomized women as denominator; arm-specific denominators are 144 and 145.

delivery.label: Additional prophylaxis
delivery.note: Twenty women started prophylactic antibiotics during the study, ten during treatment and ten during drug-free follow-up.

reports.label: Microbiology and antibiotic-resistance analysis
reports.citation: Heltveit-Olsen SR, Grude N, Arnljots ES, et al. "Microbiological findings, antibiotic resistance rates and prescription practices for older women with recurrent urinary tract infections: a descriptive study alongside a multinational randomized controlled trial (ImpresU)." *JAC Antimicrob Resist.* 2026;8(4):dlag121. doi:10.1093/jacamr/dlag121
reports.followUp: Baseline cultures and symptomatic UTI episodes across the twelve-month randomized study
reports.followUpLocator: Full text, Patients and methods (Study design; Procedures), Results (Study population; Acute UTIs)

results.endpoint: Antibiotic resistance in E. coli from symptomatic UTI cultures
results.measure: Comparison of resistance proportions in cultured E. coli isolates, adjusted for baseline resistance

values.exp: 57 E. coli isolates from acute UTI cultures
values.ctl: 50 E. coli isolates from acute UTI cultures

results.note: No significant adjusted between-arm differences for tested antibiotics; only 178/399 (45%) symptomatic UTI episodes were cultured, and susceptibility testing varied by drug.
results.locator: Microbiology report, Results (Acute UTIs, Antibiotic resistance patterns), Table 5

relations.note: ALTAR found methenamine noninferior to daily antibiotics; ImpresU cited that result and tested methenamine against placebo in older women.
